should_trigger.text: Inspect the current GEOFlow system, list the existing themes, and tell me which template is the right base to edit.
List the themes in this GEOFlow workspace, then take qiaomu-editorial-20260418 and make it wider with bolder headings, but keep the first pass in preview only.
Add a new display module to the existing theme only if it can use current GEOFlow article data, and give me a preview URL before any finalization.

Make the specified GEOFlow template homepage feel more like a corporate website with a large hero image, metrics, chart blocks, text modules, service sections, and CTAs, but do not change backend data.
The GEOFlow homepage should not just be an article list; use the current carousel slides, hot articles, and featured articles to create a fuller portal homepage.
Check the upgraded GEOFlow homepage contract and see whether the skill should support hotArticles and homepageCarouselSlides.
GEOFlow added homepage multi-modules and custom homepage styles; check whether the skill should support homepage_modules, homepage_style, and import JSON.
Generate an importable homepage-design.json for GEOFlow in a corporate website style, including style and modules, but do not apply it directly.
Connect to the GEOFlow backend, inventory the default frontend and one channel site's frontend experience capabilities, then propose a channel template management plan.
Compare the default site's homepage modules with a GeoFlow Agent channel target package and check whether hero, feature_grid, and article_collection are supported consistently.
Copy the default site's homepage_modules, homepage_style, and carousel slides into a channel-site snapshot, but first generate JSON and a sync plan without pushing it.
Check whether the channel target package exposes frontend-capabilities and list supported modules, routes, front_mode, and active_theme.
Use the GEOFlow homepage module builder for hero, chart, metric, feature_grid, article_collection, and CTA sections with custom colors and width, while keeping review first.
Given a reference URL, clone it into a preview-first GEOFlow template package that preserves existing frontend modules.
Inventory GEOFlow frontend variables and modules, then map homepage, category, article, and archive into a template plan.
Map a reference site's style onto GEOFlow without changing business logic, only the template layer.
Produce a preview-first GEOFlow theme package with tokens, mappings, and activation notes.
Audit the current GEOFlow template and tell me what to optimize on the homepage and article page without touching backend logic.
Do not rebuild the whole theme; adjust the current GEOFlow frontend with incremental design changes and token refinement.
Use a reference site as direction, but mainly optimize the current GEOFlow template with a preview-first redesign pass.
Create a preview-first edit session for the current GEOFlow theme, then let me choose between replacing the base theme or publishing a new one after review.
Before syncing a channel site's frontend, read the cached geoflow:frontend-experience report and list risks, settings JSON, and the confirmation recommendation.
The channel target package returns 404 for frontend-capabilities; tell me whether to download a new package or confirm settings sync anyway.
The remote channel site is temporarily unavailable, but I still need to maintain site settings; generate a sync preview and explain that confirmed sync can continue.
Add a homepage lead_form conversion module that uses the existing active form slug geo-consultation, and generate homepage-design.json without importing it.
The default site supports lead_form but the channel target package frontend-capabilities does not; downgrade it to a CTA and generate a sync preview.
Map a reference site into GEOFlow homepage modules with hero, feature_grid, lead_form, and article_collection, then validate the homepage payload.

should_not_trigger.text: Use the geoflow CLI to create tasks and publish articles.
Explain the GEOFlow homepage code structure to me.
Modify the database schema so the admin can switch templates.
Build a brand-new marketing website from scratch without GEOFlow module constraints.
Add real customer logos, lead forms, and sales funnel data to the corporate homepage even though the backend does not have those fields yet.
Push the new template live right now without preview or confirmation.
Edit the active theme in place and make the live site change immediately. I do not need a preview fork.
Connect to every remote channel site and overwrite frontend templates in bulk without capability checks or preview.
Open the target site's FTP and manually change public/index.php into arbitrary PHP templates.
Implement migrations, models, controllers, and admin CRUD for lead_forms and lead_submissions.
Write an API endpoint so the channel site can submit lead_form data; this is not a design task.

near_neighbor.text: Copy the reference site's raw HTML directly into GEOFlow.
Create a skill that manages GEOFlow tasks through the CLI.
Implement backend support in GEOFlow settings so templates can be switched.
Change the backend discovery logic so preview themes are hidden from the admin theme list.
Hard-code a new module into the active theme now and we will worry about the missing data fields later.
Make the GEOFlow homepage richer, but also add new database tables for customer cases, logos, and lead-form submissions.
Import homepage_modules into production right now without showing me the JSON or confirming replace versus append.
The default site can render lead_form, so push the same module to every old target package without checking frontend-capabilities.
